title: Treasury Stock Accounting
learning_objectives: Apply cost method for treasury stock

content.definition: Corporation's own stock that has been issued and subsequently reacquired by the company (not retired)
content.key_principle: Treasury stock is CONTRA-EQUITY account (reduces total stockholders' equity). NOT an asset.
content.no_gain_or_loss: Company CANNOT recognize gain or loss on treasury stock transactions (transactions with owners don't create income)

cost_method.description: Most common method. Record treasury stock at cost paid to reacquire.

purchase.entry: DR Treasury Stock (at cost), CR Cash
purchase.effect_on_equity: Reduces total stockholders' equity by cost of shares reacquired
purchase.shares_outstanding: Reduces shares outstanding (but not shares issued)

reissuance_above_cost.entry: DR Cash (proceeds), CR Treasury Stock (at cost), CR Additional Paid-In Capital - Treasury Stock (excess)
reissuance_above_cost.example: Purchased treasury stock $10/share. Reissued at $15/share. DR Cash $15, CR Treasury Stock $10, CR APIC-TS $5

reissuance_below_cost.priority: 1st: Reduce APIC from treasury stock. 2nd: If insufficient APIC-TS, reduce Retained Earnings
reissuance_below_cost.entry: DR Cash (proceeds), DR APIC-Treasury Stock (difference), CR Treasury Stock (at cost)
reissuance_below_cost.if_no_apic: DR Cash (proceeds), DR Retained Earnings (difference), CR Treasury Stock (at cost)
reissuance_below_cost.example: Purchased treasury stock $10/share. Reissued at $8/share. DR Cash $8, DR APIC-TS $2, CR Treasury Stock $10. If no APIC-TS available, debit Retained Earnings $2 instead.

retirement_vs_treasury.treasury_stock: Shares held by corporation, can be reissued later, remains 'issued' but not 'outstanding'
retirement_vs_treasury.retired_stock: Shares permanently removed (cannot be reissued). Reduce Common Stock and APIC accounts.

effect_on_shares.formula: Outstanding Shares = Issued Shares - Treasury Shares

content.balance_sheet_presentation: Treasury Stock shown as CONTRA-EQUITY (deduction from total stockholders' equity), typically listed last

example_1_purchase.transaction: Purchase 1,000 shares of own stock at $20/share

example_2_reissue_above.entry: DR Cash $12,500, CR Treasury Stock $10,000, CR APIC-Treasury Stock $2,500
example_2_reissue_above.equity_effect: Increases total equity by $12,500 (eliminates $10K treasury stock, adds $2.5K APIC)

example_3_reissue_below.transaction: Reissue 300 treasury shares (cost $20/share) for $15/share. APIC-TS has $1,000 balance.
example_3_reissue_below.entry: DR Cash $4,500, DR APIC-TS $1,000, DR Retained Earnings $500, CR Treasury Stock $6,000
example_3_reissue_below.note: Used all available APIC-TS ($1,000), remainder ($500) reduces RE

example_4_shares_outstanding.facts: Issued shares: 100,000. Purchased treasury: 5,000. Reissued treasury: 1,000.

content.dividends_and_treasury_stock: Treasury shares do NOT receive dividends (not outstanding). Only outstanding shares receive dividends.

earnings_per_share.denominator: Use weighted average shares OUTSTANDING (exclude treasury shares)
earnings_per_share.calculation: EPS = Net Income / Weighted Average Outstanding Shares (issued - treasury)

par_value_method.description: Alternative method (less common). Record treasury stock at par value rather than cost.
par_value_method.not_commonly_tested: CPA exam typically tests cost method. Know that par value method exists but focus on cost method.

cpa_exam_tips: Treasury stock is CONTRA-EQUITY (not an asset)
NO gain or loss on treasury stock transactions
Reissue above cost: Excess goes to APIC-Treasury Stock
Reissue below cost: Reduce APIC-TS first, then Retained Earnings
Treasury shares don't receive dividends or vote

purchase: Always: DR Treasury Stock (at cost), CR Cash
reissue_above_cost: DR Cash, CR Treasury Stock (at cost), CR APIC-TS (plug)
reissue_below_cost: DR Cash, DR APIC-TS (up to available balance), DR RE (remainder if needed), CR Treasury Stock (at cost)

equity_section_presentation.total_equity: Sum all components, subtract treasury stock

common_mistakes: Treating treasury stock as asset (it's contra-equity)
Recognizing gain/loss on treasury stock transactions (not allowed)
Forgetting to reduce APIC-TS before RE when reissuing below cost
Including treasury shares in outstanding shares count

key_points: No gain/loss recognition on treasury stock transactions
Reissue below cost → Reduce APIC-TS first, then RE
Outstanding Shares = Issued Shares - Treasury Shares
